items.title: Curiosity rover detects 'origin-of-life' molecules on Mars

featured_image.name: Non-biologic Processes Don't Fully Explain Mars Organics

items.description: NASA's Curiosity rover has detected more than 20 organic molecules in clay-rich Martian rock, including compounds never before seen on the Red Planet, according to a study published on April 21 in the journal Nature Communications. The findings, drawn from a first-of-its-kind chemical experiment conducted remotely on Mars, offer fresh clues in the decades-long search for signs of ancient life beyond Earth.[1][2]

items.title: Rio Tinto posts higher Q1 iron ore sales, warns on Middle East risks

featured_image.name: Rio Tinto BHP Pilbara Iron Ore Partnership 200Mt Deal

items.description: Rio Tinto reported a 2.4% rise in first-quarter iron ore sales on Tuesday but cautioned that the ongoing conflict in the Middle East could disrupt its supply chains in the second half of 2026. The world's largest iron ore producer sold 72.4 million metric tons from its Pilbara operations in Western Australia during the three months ended March 31, up from 70.7 million tons a year earlier, though below the Visible Alpha consensus estimate of 74.6 million tons.[1][2]

items.title: Japan scraps postwar ban on lethal weapons exports

featured_image.name: Japan's ruling party elects Sanae Takaichi as new leader ...

items.description: Japan's Cabinet on Tuesday approved the most sweeping overhaul of the country's defense export rules in decades, scrapping restrictions that had confined arms sales to non-combat equipment since the end of World War II. The decision opens the door for Japanese manufacturers to sell fighter jets, missiles, warships, and other lethal weapons on the global market for the first time.

items.title: SpaceX begins Wall Street analyst briefings ahead of record $75B IPO

featured_image.name: SpaceX files confidentially for IPO targeting $1.75 trillion valuation

items.description:
SpaceX kicked off three days of private analyst meetings on Monday at its Starbase launch site in Boca Chica, Texas, as Elon Musk's rocket and satellite company moves closer to what would be the largest initial public offering in history, Reuters reported.[1][2]

The briefings, aimed at Wall Street's top aerospace and technology analysts, mark a key milestone in SpaceX's push to raise up to $75 billion and begin trading by late June. Executives are expected to lead an all-day meeting and tour at Starbase before offering analysts a visit to SpaceX's "Macrohard" xAI datacenter in Memphis, Tennessee, on April 23.[3][4][2]

items.title: Oil dips as Iran agrees to join U.S. peace talks in Islamabad

featured_image.name: US-Iran direct talks on ending war under way in Pakistan

items.description: Oil prices fell on Tuesday as expectations grew that the United States and Iran would resume peace negotiations in Pakistan this week, raising hopes for an easing of supply disruptions in the Middle East. The decline came after a volatile Monday session that saw crude surge on renewed tensions over the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Clean energy outpaced global electricity demand growth in 2025, Ember finds

featured_image.name: The State of Clean Energy, in 10 Charts - World Resources Institute

items.description:
Clean energy generation outpaced global electricity demand growth for the first time in 2025, powered by record solar expansion in China and India, according to energy think tank Ember's Global Electricity Review 2026, released on Monday.[1][2]

Clean power generation grew 887 terawatt hours last year, exceeding overall global electricity demand growth of 849 terawatt hours, the report found. Solar energy, which grew 30% in 2025, alone met three-quarters of the net rise in electricity demand, and combined with wind power generation, met 99% of it.[3][1]

items.title: Asian markets trade mixed as U.S.-Iran ceasefire set to expire Tuesday night

featured_image.name: Asian markets track Wall St down with Nvidia, US jobs in view

items.description:
Oil prices dipped and Asian stock markets traded in mixed fashion on Tuesday as uncertainty deepened over the fate of peace negotiations between the United States and Iran, with a two-week ceasefire set to expire Tuesday evening Eastern time.

Brent crude slipped 0.4% while U.S. benchmark crude fell 0.9% in early Asian trading, according to the Associated Press. The declines came as traders weighed the possibility of fresh diplomatic talks in Islamabad against rising tensions, including the U.S. Navy's recent seizure of an Iranian cargo vessel in the Strait of Hormuz.[1][2][3][4]
